- When sentiment is consistently negative (avg < -0.3) over recent days, model tends to overcorrect downward → reduce forecast dip depth or add slight upward bias.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 73), model often overshoots → cap forecast at +5–10% above peak or adjust downward 2–3 days post-spike.
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days falling from 72+), model overestimates continuation → reduce forecast slope or add early reversal signal.
- When sentiment is neutral or mildly positive (avg > -0.1), model often underestimates downside risk → add 1–2% buffer below forecast for 3–5 days ahead.
- Forecast horizon > 14 days shows persistent lag → model underreacts to sentiment shifts → adjust forecast to align with sentiment trend 2–3 days ahead.
- If sentiment history shows repeated “recovery” patterns (e.g., -0.5 → -0.1 → 0.0), model often fails to capture early rebound → increase forecast slope or add 1–2% upward bias in 3–5 day window.
